meta.rounding: Every dollar figure on the public site is rounded to the nearest $10. Owner-supplied figures are the owner's own records and are labelled unverified where no official public record was checked.
meta.privacy: No name, street address, parcel number, postal code, trust detail or utility account appears in this file. Placeholders: Property A (the home being inherited) and Property B (the three-unit building already owned by the heir). The two jurisdictions are named here and on the public pages: Santa Clara County for Property A and the City and County of San Francisco for Property B. A county or a city is not a personal identifier, and naming the jurisdiction is what makes each local rate checkable against the publisher that sets it. What is still withheld is the city inside the county, the parcel's tax rate area, the street address and the utility accounts, and that residual disclosure is stated on the dashboard.

ad_valorem_rate_a.basis: Assumption, not a fitted result. The owner's own bills cannot separate the two parts of the bill: assessed value and the fixed charges both grow at about 2% a year, so any rate between roughly 1.05% and 1.60% fits the data almost equally well. 1.18% is used because Proposition 13 limits the rate to 1% plus voter-approved bond debt, because the published San Francisco rate is 1.18162182%, and because it puts the fixed part of the bill at a plausible level. The property's tax rate area is not published on this site, so this is flagged for review.

ad_valorem_rate_b.basis: Published by the City and County of San Francisco for fiscal year 2026-27.

fixed_charge_growth.basis: Fixed charges are projected at the modelled inflation rate. Diagnostic: the fixed part of the Property B bill grew at 8.1% a year between 2016 and 2025, so this projection is deliberately conservative and understates the bill if that pace continues.

house_growth.basis: Scenario band. The FHFA all-transactions index for Property A's area compounded at 6.9% a year from 1976 to 2025 but 3.3% a year over the last twenty years, so the baseline sits below the long run.

inflation.basis: Scenario band anchored on the 2026 Social Security Trustees intermediate assumption of 2.4% for the CPI-W, with the low and high cases taken from the Trustees' high-cost and low-cost assumptions. The 1975-2024 CPI-U compounded at 3.6% a year and the last twenty years at 2.6% a year.

equity_return_nominal_gross.basis: Scenario band. No official agency publishes an equity return assumption, so this is a stated scenario and not an official figure.

equity_tax_drag.basis: Assumption for dividend and turnover tax on a taxable brokerage account.

treasury_yield_nominal.basis: The 2026 Trustees intermediate assumption of a 2.3% real new-issue rate for 2044 and later plus 2.4% CPI-W gives about 4.7% nominal; the low and high cases use the Trustees' high-cost and low-cost pairs. The 2025 annual average 10-year yield was 4.29%.

prop19_cap_growth.basis: Assumption. The cap is reset every second February by the change in the California House Price Index, so its future path is not published. The low case holds it frozen at today's amount.

selling_cost_pct.basis: Assumption for commission, escrow, title and transfer charges. Verified component: the county's documentary transfer tax is $0.55 per $500 of real property value, and three named cities in the county add a further $1.65 per $500. The city for Property A is not established, so only the county rate can be confirmed here; whether a city conveyance tax also applies to it is flagged for review.

assessed_value_growth.basis: The Proposition 13 inflation cap has been binding in every year of both assessment rolls supplied by the owner.

combined_gain_tax_rate.basis: Assumption for a high-income California seller with no offsetting losses: 20% federal capital gains plus 3.8% net investment income tax plus the 13.3% California top marginal rate, with no federal deduction taken for the state tax. State and federal rates are simply added, which is deliberately conservative.

depreciation_recapture_rate.basis: Assumption: 25% federal unrecaptured section 1250 rate plus the 13.3% California top rate, plus NIIT where applicable.
